title: Soft agar colony formation assay for mouse embryonic fibroblast transformation post Salmonella infection
author: Stévenin, Neefjes

steps.title: Determine optimal MOI
steps.instruction: Perform a gentamicin protection assay to establish the multiplicity of infection (MOI) appropriate for the Salmonella strain and mouse embryonic fibroblasts before proceeding with the experiment.

steps.title: Prepare plate formats
steps.instruction: Use a 12‑well plate for cell infection and a 6‑well plate for soft‑agar colony formation; this layout typically yields ~10² colonies per well. If transformation efficiency is higher, reduce the number of cells seeded in soft agar by a factor of 2–10 while keeping the 6‑well format. Always include a non‑infected negative control.

steps.title: Maintain MEF cells in culture
steps.instruction: Keep mouse embryonic fibroblasts in DMEM + 10 % fetal bovine serum (FBS) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; cells must have been cultured for at least 10 days (≥2 passages) and remain below 20 passages. Avoid overcrowding or starvation and split regularly at ~80 % confluence. (Optional: 8 % FBS can be used after testing).

steps.title: Plate cells for infection
steps.instruction: Two days before infection, trypsinize and count the cells (≈30 min). Seed 5 × 10⁴ cells per well of a 12‑well plate in 1.5 mL of complete medium; allocate two wells per experimental condition (e.g., four wells for infected and non‑infected controls). Incubate the plate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 2 days.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 × 10⁴ cells to each well with 1.5 mL DMEM + 10 % FBS.
Use two wells per condition (e.g., four wells total).

steps.title: Analyze colonies with GelCount
steps.instruction: Open GelCount software and load acquisition files via “File → Open Multiple Plates/Dishes”. Add all plate files, define well masks with the green circles (avoid gel border/shadow), and apply the mask to all wells. Open “Optimizer” to run automatic colony detection, adjust settings for colony size and density, and confirm with “Ok”. Choose “Recount all” to count colonies uniformly; the counts appear in the left column. Manually delete false positives (dust) by holding Ctrl and right‑clicking on the unwanted detection. Count at least three wells per condition, then export the data for statistical analysis (e.g., unpaired t‑test) in Excel or Prism.

substeps.instruction: Press File → Open Multiple Plates/Dishes and add all acquisition files.
Select well masks using the green circles, avoiding gel border/shadow.
Press Tools → Apply this Mask to all (reposition if needed).
Press Optimizer to open automatic colony detection.
Adjust detection settings for colony size/density and click Ok.
Press the arrow next to Recount and select Recount all.
Record colony numbers from the left column.
Manually delete false positives by holding Ctrl and right‑clicking on dust artifacts.
Repeat for at least three wells per condition.
Export data for statistical analysis (e.g., unpaired t‑test).
